# `shell/WindowStateStore.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/shell/WindowStateStore.js`

WindowStateStore.js — Persist and restore per-app window position/size. Stored in an account-qualified localStorage key as a versioned envelope whose `states` field maps appId → state. The historical global `os.windowStates` record remains read-only and non-authoritative. LegacyOperatorMigration may use it once as a validated seed when exactly one Realm Passport can own it. Validates a restored state before using it. Corrupt or unreasonable values are ignored; valid off-screen geometry is clamped back into the current work area so the window remains reachable after a display or taskbar change.

## Functions

### `configureWindowStateOperator(currentOperatorScope, { storage = undefined } = {})`

Configure the legacy free-function facade with one live OperatorContext provider. This facade never consults the old global `os.windowStates` key. The kernel-owned one-time migration is the only validated seed path.

### `createWindowStateStore(options)`

### `legacyWindowStateQuarantine(storage = undefined)`

Report only the presence of the retained, non-authoritative legacy record.

### `validateState(state)`

Validate a saved state for corruption only (finite, positive size). Position reachability is no longer a reject reason — clampToViewport() moves an off-screen window back into view instead of discarding the saved state.

### `clampToViewport(state)`

Reposition a state so a reachable strip of its titlebar stays inside the work area. Handles smaller screens / resolution changes / disconnected monitors — the window is pulled back on-screen rather than left unclickable.

### `clampStateSize(state)`

Clamp a state's width and height so neither falls below 15% nor exceeds 100% of the available desktop area.  Position is preserved as-is.

### `loadState(appId, options = null)`

Load the saved window state for an app. Returns null when nothing is stored yet.

### `saveState(appId, state, options = null)`

Persist the current window state for an app.

### `clearState(appId, options = null)`

Remove the saved window state for an app (e.g. after a reset).

### `clearAllStates(options = null)`

Remove every persisted window geometry record.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
